manifest.name: Payment Provider: AsiaPay
manifest.summary: An payment provider based in Hong Kong covering most Asian countries.

models._description: Payment Provider (AsiaPay credentials: brand / merchant id / secure-hash secret / secure-hash function)

asiapay_secure_hash_function (Selection sha1/sha256/sha512, required_if_provider=asiapay, default sha1; selects the hash algorithm for the signature)

relations: no new fields; 5 methods overriding payment's reference/rendering/notification hooks

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on the base.group_system field group guarding asiapay_secure_hash_secret (brand / merchant id / hash function are left ungrouped).

views.note: xml_loc=67: payment.provider form inheritance (AsiaPay brand / merchant id / secure-hash secret / secure-hash function) + the QWeb redirect-form template payment_asiapay_templates.xml (auto-submit POST form to the AsiaPay/PayDollar payForm with merchantId/amount/orderRef/currCode/mpsMode/successUrl/failUrl/cancelUrl/payType/lang/payMethod/secureHash), plus data/payment_provider_data.xml wiring redirect_form_view_id. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> hidden-field POST redirect to the AsiaPay/PayDollar payForm (per-brand host, e.g. https://www.paydollar.com/b2c2/eng/payment/payForm.jsp; sandbox https://test.paydollar.com/b2cDemo/eng/payment/payForm.jsp)
behavioral_notes.observation: AsiaPay is a pure hosted-redirect acquirer: there is NO server-to-server payment API call. _get_specific_rendering_values builds the payForm payload (merchant_id=asiapay_merchant_id, amount=tx.amount, reference=tx.reference, currency_code=const.CURRENCY_MAPPING[available_currency_ids[0].name] -- the ISO 4217 ALPHA code is translated to AsiaPay's NUMERIC code, e.g. HKD->344, USD->840; mps_mode='SCP'; return_url=base_url+/payment/asiapay/return; payment_type='N' (normal sale); language via payment_utils.get_language_code(context lang or 'en_US', const.LANGUAGE_CODES_MAPPING) -> single-letter AsiaPay code e.g. E/C/J; payment_method=const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING.get(method.code,'ALL')). It then signs the dict via provider._asiapay_calculate_signature(rendering_values, incoming=False) and adds api_url=provider._asiapay_get_api_url() (live vs test by provider.state AND brand). The values feed the redirect_form QWeb template whose hidden inputs (merchantId/orderRef/currCode/payType/lang/payMethod/secureHash + successUrl/failUrl/cancelUrl all = return_url) auto-POST the browser to the hosted payForm. The per-brand endpoint, the numeric currency/language/method translations, and the signed-form handoff are invisible to Python model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._asiapay_calculate_signature -> configurable SHA1/SHA256/SHA512 signing with pipe-delimited ordered keys + shared secret
behavioral_notes.observation: _asiapay_calculate_signature builds the signature from a FIXED, ORDERED key list (const.SIGNATURE_KEYS: outgoing = [merchant_id, reference, currency_code, amount, payment_type]; incoming = [src, prc, successcode, Ref, PayRef, Cur, Amt, payerAuth]), appends asiapay_secure_hash_secret as the final element, joins everything with the '|' pipe separator, then hashes with hashlib.new(asiapay_secure_hash_function) -- i.e. SHA1, SHA256 or SHA512 chosen per provider via the asiapay_secure_hash_function field (default sha1) -- and returns .hexdigest(). The signed value list is direction-dependent (outgoing for the redirect form, incoming for the webhook), and crucially the algorithm itself is account-configurable, not hard-coded. This pipe-delimited, ordered-key, variable-digest scheme (not an HMAC) is pure code semantics, not derivable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: AsiaPayController.asiapay_return_from_checkout (/payment/asiapay/return, GET, no-op) vs asiapay_webhook (/payment/asiapay/webhook, POST) -> _verify_signature(incoming) BEFORE _process; reference via _extract_reference -> 'Ref'
behavioral_notes.observation: The trust model is asymmetric. The redirect-return route /payment/asiapay/return (GET, public) does NOT process the payment: it deliberately just redirects to /payment/status, because the return data carry no valuable info beyond the reference and AsiaPay exposes no API to fetch authoritative data. ALL settlement therefore flows through the webhook /payment/asiapay/webhook (POST, public, csrf=False): it _search_by_reference('asiapay', data) (via _extract_reference -> data['Ref']), then calls _verify_signature BEFORE _process. _verify_signature reads data['secureHash'] and rejects with werkzeug Forbidden (HTTP 403) when it is missing or when hmac.compare_digest(received, provider._asiapay_calculate_signature(data, incoming=True)) fails -- a constant-time compare against the SHA recomputed (with the configured function) over the incoming key list. On success tx_sudo._process('asiapay', data) runs (validate amount via _extract_amount_data, then _apply_updates); the webhook returns 'OK'. So unlike acquirers whose return route is authoritative, AsiaPay's final state is established ONLY by the signed webhook.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -> AsiaPay successcode -> payment state mapping
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates stamps provider_reference = payment_data['PayRef'], resolves the payment method from payment_data['payMethod'] via payment.method._get_from_code(..., mapping=const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING) (falling back to the current method), then maps AsiaPay's successcode through const.SUCCESS_CODE_MAPPING into payment's guarded transitions: '0' -> _set_done; '1' -> _set_error (carrying both successcode and the primary response code 'prc'); a missing successcode raises ValidationError('missing success code'); any other code -> _set_error('Unknown success code'). Note there is NO pending and NO cancel state -- AsiaPay's binary success/failure maps only to done/error. _extract_amount_data reads payment_data['Amt'] and uses the account's single available currency (AsiaPay supports exactly one currency per account) for the engine's amount cross-check. This inbound code->state translation is pure code, not visible in metadata.

@api.constrains('available_currency_ids','state') enforces two AsiaPay rules at write time: (1) a non-disabled AsiaPay provider may have AT MOST ONE available currency (ValidationError 'Only one currency can be selected by AsiaPay account.'), because the redirect payload sends a single currCode taken from available_currency_ids[0]; and (2) every selected currency must be in const.CURRENCY_MAPPING (the ~22 ISO codes AsiaPay supports, each mapped to a numeric code) else ValidationError listing the unsupported currencies. _get_default_payment_method_codes returns const.DEFAULT_PAYMENT_METHOD_CODES (card + visa/mastercard/amex/discover) when AsiaPay is activated. This currency-cardinality + allow-list policy is enforced in code, not visible as plain field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- per-brand endpoints, hash secret, no API key
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=false; the declared endpoints are the AsiaPay/PayDollar hosted payForm pages for each brand, live and sandbox -- production www.{paydollar,pesopay,siampay,bimopay}.com/b2c2/eng/payment/payForm.jsp and test test.{paydollar,pesopay,siampay}.com/b2cDemo/eng/payment/payForm.jsp -- declared in const.py (API_URLS) and selected by provider.state + asiapay_brand in _asiapay_get_api_url (falling back to paydollar). There is NO outbound REST client and NO bearer/api-key auth: AsiaPay is reached purely by the browser POSTing the signed hidden-field payForm, and AsiaPay notifies Odoo's webhook (the return route is a no-op). Authenticity rests entirely on the secure-hash secret + the configured hash function (asiapay_secure_hash_secret / asiapay_secure_hash_function), not on a transport-level key. This redirect-only, multi-brand acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches (gap #3). payment_asiapay ships no client-side code: the entire buyer interaction is the server-rendered redirect_form QWeb template (payment_asiapay_templates.xml) whose hidden inputs auto-submit to the AsiaPay/PayDollar payForm. There is no browser SDK and no inline card form -- card/wallet data are collected on AsiaPay's hosted page, never in Odoo. The only browser-visible artifact is the auto-POST redirect form (plain server-rendered HTML, no gap-#3 JS surface).

it_architecture.application: payment_asiapay (AsiaPay / PayDollar acquirer adapter for the payment engine; _inherit-only, no own models/views)
software_services: /payment/asiapay/return (redirect-return, http GET: NO-OP -- only redirects to /payment/status; carries no authoritative data)
/payment/asiapay/webhook (async notification, http POST, csrf=False: secureHash-verified, processes, returns 'OK' -- the sole settlement path)
data_objects: payment.transaction (AsiaPay hosted-redirect payForm flow; no new fields; 5 override methods)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> payment.provider (provider_id; provider_code=='asiapay' gates every override)
payment.provider.available_currency_ids constrained to exactly one currency, within const.CURRENCY_MAPPING
external: payment.transaction.reference == AsiaPay orderRef/'Ref' (cross-system key for webhook lookup via _extract_reference)
information_flows: depends: payment (inherits the provider/transaction engine + redirect-form rendering + _process state machine)

outbound (redirect): _get_specific_rendering_values -> signed hidden-field POST form -> browser auto-submit to the per-brand AsiaPay/PayDollar payForm (www.paydollar.com/... etc.; sandbox test.*) -- no server-to-server API call

inbound (webhook): AsiaPay -> POST /payment/asiapay/webhook -> _verify_signature (configured SHA1/256/512 over the incoming key list, constant-time compare) -> _process -> payment state machine (the only settlement path)
no tokenization / no refund / no capture / no void flows in this module
frontend_components: redirect_form QWeb template (payment_asiapay_templates.xml; server-rendered hidden-field auto-POST form to the AsiaPay/PayDollar payForm; no JS/OWL)

external_integrations.sdk: none (no python SDK and no browser SDK; card/wallet data entered on AsiaPay's hosted payForm, never in Odoo)
external_integrations.auth: no transport key; authenticity via a configurable-digest (SHA1/SHA256/SHA512) signature over a fixed pipe-delimited key list + asiapay_secure_hash_secret; secureHash field on incoming, secure_hash on outgoing
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration in its hosted-redirect form, with a per-brand twist. There is NO outbound REST/API-key channel -- the browser POSTs a server-signed hidden-field payForm to one of four AsiaPay brand hosts (PayDollar / PesoPay / SiamPay / BimoPay; live or sandbox by provider.state), the buyer pays on AsiaPay, and AsiaPay notifies /payment/asiapay/webhook (the /return route is a no-op), verified by recomputing the signature with the configured hash function over the incoming key list. The base 'payment' engine ships no live acquirer; this module is that override, contrasting with Stripe/Xendit by being redirect-only (no S2S API, no tokenization) and with a webhook-only (not return-route) settlement.
external_integrations.note: Gap-#7 example with no API key and an account-configurable hash algorithm: none of the per-brand payForm endpoints, the numeric currency/language/method translations, or the pipe-delimited SHA1/256/512 signing are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading const.py + payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py.

capabilities: Accept Card payments via AsiaPay/PayDollar hosted redirect across Hong Kong and most Asian markets
Multi-brand acquiring (PayDollar / PesoPay / SiamPay / BimoPay) selected per provider account
Wide local Asian payment-method acceptance (Alipay, WeChat Pay, FPS, Octopus, GCash, Maya, DANA, OVO, QRIS, TrueMoney, Touch'n Go, ShopeePay, UnionPay, ...) mapped to AsiaPay method codes, else 'ALL'
Signed-redirect settlement with an account-configurable hash algorithm (SHA1/SHA256/SHA512) and no card data in Odoo
Single-currency-per-account acceptance across ~22 supported currencies (translated to AsiaPay numeric codes)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (redirect): initiate tx -> _get_specific_rendering_values builds the signed payForm -> browser auto-POST to the per-brand AsiaPay host -> buyer pays on AsiaPay -> async POST /payment/asiapay/webhook (secureHash-verified) -> _process -> state machine done/error (the /return route only redirects to /payment/status)
Settle: successcode '0' -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)
information_concepts: payment.provider (AsiaPay credentials: brand, merchant id, secure-hash secret, secure-hash function)
payment.transaction (mapped to an AsiaPay payForm order; keyed by orderRef/'Ref'=reference, provider_reference='PayRef')
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; asiapay_secure_hash_secret is restricted to base.group_system; brand / merchant id / hash function and everything else inherit payment's groups/record rules)
policies: Inbound authenticity: webhook data must pass _verify_signature (configured SHA over the incoming pipe-delimited key list + secret, constant-time hmac.compare_digest) or are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden
The redirect-return route is intentionally non-authoritative (no-op) -- final state is established only by the signed webhook
Exactly one available currency per AsiaPay account, and only currencies in const.CURRENCY_MAPPING, enforced by @api.constrains (else ValidationError)
References are singularized and capped at 35 characters (_compute_reference) to satisfy AsiaPay's uniqueness + length limits
Amounts sent in major units with the currency as a numeric AsiaPay code; language reduced to a single-letter AsiaPay code
Secure-hash secret gated by base.group_system field group
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the AsiaPay account, merchant id, hash secret & brand)
AsiaPay (external acquirer / PSP based in Hong Kong, operating PayDollar / PesoPay / SiamPay / BimoPay)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_asiapay is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the Asian cardholder/wallet user and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to AsiaPay's (PayDollar/PesoPay/SiamPay/BimoPay) payment network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (brand selection, merchant id, secure-hash secret + algorithm management, per-method and single-currency enablement), service provisioning (building and signing the per-transaction payForm redirect and confirming the signed webhook), and infrastructure operation (the hosted-redirect handoff to the per-brand AsiaPay host plus the signature-verified webhook settlement loop -- the return route being a deliberate no-op). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its AsiaPay realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe / payment_xendit metamodels (network/support) and the parent payment engine; like APS, AsiaPay is a redirect-only acquirer (no S2S API, no tokenization), distinguished by its multi-brand host selection, account-configurable hash algorithm, and webhook-only settlement.

standard_capabilities: hosted-redirect payForm payment via AsiaPay (per-brand host: PayDollar / PesoPay / SiamPay / BimoPay; live vs sandbox by provider.state)
wide local Asian payment-method routing (Alipay / WeChat Pay / FPS / Octopus / GCash / Maya / DANA / OVO / QRIS / TrueMoney / UnionPay / ... mapped to AsiaPay codes, default 'ALL')
signed-redirect integrity and signature-verified settlement with an account-configurable hash algorithm (SHA1/SHA256/SHA512)
asynchronous settlement via a secureHash-verified webhook (the redirect-return route is a deliberate no-op)
single-currency-per-account acceptance across ~22 supported currencies (translated to AsiaPay numeric codes)
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card or local-wallet payments in HK and across Asia via AsiaPay
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
merchants needing card acceptance without holding card data (AsiaPay-hosted payForm, nothing entered in Odoo)
single-currency regional checkouts (the per-account single-currency constraint suits one-market merchants)
common_gaps: no server-to-server API: only the hosted-redirect payForm flow is implemented (no direct/S2S charge, no inline form)
no tokenization / saved cards (no _extract_token_values, no off-session recurring) -- every payment is a fresh redirect
no manual capture / authorize-then-capture, no void, and no in-module refund operation
no pending and no cancel state mapping -- successcode is binary ('0'->done, '1'/other->error), so authorize/hold and explicit cancellations are not represented

the redirect-return route does NOT finalize state and AsiaPay exposes no fetch API, so a reachable webhook URL (tunnel in dev) is mandatory; without the secure-hash secret set, verification has no secret to compare against
exactly one currency per account is allowed (multi-currency requires multiple provider records); bespoke reconciliation lives downstream (account_payment, sale)

Real-world distribution of AsiaPay transaction states, brand split (PayDollar/PesoPay/SiamPay/BimoPay), and chosen hash function (sha1 vs sha256/sha512) -- no runtime row counts captured.
How refunds / cancellations are handled operationally given no in-module refund override and no pending/cancel-state mapping (likely via the AsiaPay merchant console or a downstream module).
